text:
alice_support: FYI, ticket from @jess_customer — streaming responses cut off for some of their users. They see partial SSE payloads then client reconnects. Attaching customer's repro below.

jess_customer: Hey team — we have a consistent repro on our staging behind an ALB -> nginx -> redwood. After ~45-65s of silence the SSE stream gets a partial event and the client reconnects. Repro steps:
1) Start a long-running streaming request to /v1/chat/stream with text/event-stream.
2) Keep the stream idle for ~1m (no tokens emitted).
3) Client sees truncated last event and then network error / closed.

Example curl I used:
```
curl -v --http2 -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  "https://staging.example.com/v1/chat/stream" --no-buffer
```

Observed behavior: sometimes the last chunk ends with incomplete "data: {\"delta\":..." and the connection is reset. Logs show upstream closed.

sam_engineer: Thanks. Do you have the nginx conf snippet and ALB idle timeout value?

jess_customer: nginx config (proxying to redwood at 127.0.0.1:8080):
```
server {
  listen 443 ssl http2;
  location /v1/chat/stream {
    proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8080;
    proxy_buffering off;
    proxy_http_version 1.1;
    proxy_set_header Connection "";
    proxy_read_timeout 300s;
    chunked_transfer_encoding on;
  }
}
```
ALB idle timeout is 60s (default).

natalie_infra: Couple red flags: ALB default idle is 60s and will close idle connections. Also note http2 between client and nginx, but nginx->upstream is http1.1 which should be fine but some nginx versions will buffer responses if proxy_buffering not set correctly or if "proxy_set_header Connection \"\";" is missing. Client used --http2; that only affects front door.

sam_engineer: The partial event + reset sounds like upstream closed while proxy still thought more data incoming. Can you grep nginx error.log for "upstream prematurely closed"? Also check redwood logs for connection close reasons.

jess_customer: Found this in nginx error.log around the time: 
```
[error] 2312#0: *412 upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream, client: 10.0.0.5, server: staging, request: "GET /v1/chat/stream HTTP/1.1", upstream: "http://127.0.0.1:8080/", host: "staging.example.com"
```

deploy-bot: Deploy completed: redwood-server@2026.02.18-rc4 (commit abcdef)

sam_engineer: That log is consistent with the app (redwood) closing the connection. Could be the app's idle writer timing out or runtime OOM. What do redwood logs show? Any 502/504s from nginx?

jess_customer: On redwood side we see: 
```
WARN: http2: upstream write failed: write tcp 127.0.0.1:8080->127.0.0.1:xxx: use of closed network connection
INFO: session closed after 62s of idle
```
Not a real error in app logs, looks like it believed stream should end.

natalie_infra: Another thing: ALB will terminate idle TCP after its idle timeout even if there are no bytes. If ALB closes the connection, nginx sees EOF from client and may close upstream. Flow: client <-> ALB <-> nginx <-> redwood. If ALB idle hits first, it sends TCP FIN to client side of the connection but nginx might still be trying to read/write to upstream and then get ECONNRESET.

sam_engineer: Workaround to try: 1) increase ALB idle timeout to e.g. 350s for streaming routes; 2) ensure nginx is configured to send keepalives to client (http2) or inject periodic SSE comments from server so there is always some bytes; 3) set proxy_http_version 1.1 and proxy_set_header Connection "" (looks present); 4) verify proxy_send_timeout/proxy_read_timeout are longer than ALB idle.

jess_customer: Tried 1 & 3. Increased ALB to 300s and set proxy_read_timeout 360s. Still saw a reconnect after ~65s for some clients only (mobile carriers). One odd thing: when we disabled HTTP/2 on nginx (listen 443 ssl; removed http2), issues reduced.

natalie_infra: Mobile carriers and some intermediate proxies will coalesce or enforce shorter timeouts. Also HTTP/2 multiplexing can interact oddly with intermediate proxies if they proxy at layer 4 (some carriers treat http2 differently). Disabling http2 makes the client->nginx link http/1.1 and may change behavior.

sam_engineer: Two other items to test quickly: a) have server send periodic SSE comment lines every 15s: ": keepalive\n\n" to keep ALB/carries alive; b) add this to nginx location: `proxy_buffering off; proxy_ignore_client_abort off; proxy_set_header Connection ""; tcp_nodelay on;` Also consider `keepalive_timeout 120s;` at http block.

jess_customer: I pushed a quick change to emit a comment line every 20s from app; after that the streams were stable for >10min during manual tests. But a subset of real users still experienced disconnects.

sam_engineer: If keepalive comments fixed most but not all, likely some middleboxes are rewriting or tearing http2 sessions. For those, fallback to http/1.1 on edge (disable http2) or use WebSocket as an alternative.

natalie_infra: There's also the ALB vs NLB choice. ALB speaks HTTP and will respect 60s idle. NLB is L4 and will preserve TCP level without HTTP semantics — but NLB has no idle timeout control? NLB has default 350s? (need to check). If you can move to NLB + TLS passthrough to nginx, you might bypass some HTTP-aware intermediaries.

sam_engineer: Action items:
- jess_customer: keep ALB idle increased for staging to 300s and try 1wk of traffic.
- jess_customer: keep the SSE comment heartbeat (20s) while we investigate.
- natalie_infra: check if any Cloudflare/third-party proxies in front of ALB for those user IPs.
- sam_engineer: add more verbose redwood stream-close reasons and emit a final JSON event when stream intentionally ends (helps distinguish app vs network).

jess_customer: Will do. Also attaching a client-side stacktrace for one mobile disconnect: "Stream ended unexpectedly: ECONNRESET after 62s".

sam_engineer: One more diagnostic: try `curl --http2 -H "Accept: text/event-stream" --no-buffer` from a remote EC2 in same AZ as ALB to reproduce from network that matches user. If not reproducible, likely ISP middlebox.

natalie_infra: FYI I checked VPC flow logs for one failing session — ALB did tear down the connection at 60s record. So that aligns. For long-term, recommend: either set ALB idle to >300s for streaming routes or move streaming endpoints behind NLB or CloudFront with longer idle.

jess_customer: Appreciate the help. We'll keep the SSE heartbeat for now and prepare a plan to migrate the endpoint to an NLB-backed target group for streaming.

alice_support: Thanks everyone — I'll keep this thread open until migration confirmed. Reopen if you need more logs.
